name: Temple Upward Bound and Upward Bound Math & Science
org: Temple University College of Education and Human Development
what_you_do: College prep all year. There is tutoring after school on weekdays, Saturday classes, college visits and a six-week summer program on campus. One track focuses on civic work and one on STEM.
who_can_apply: Students in 9th or 10th grade at Philadelphia public district or charter high schools. They come from low-income families, or their parents do not have a bachelor degree, or both. They also plan to go to college. Five named schools get priority. They are Benjamin Franklin HS, Dobbins CTE, Gratz Mastery, Strawberry Mansion and The U School. The FAQ says you must also live in Philadelphia.
pay_detail: Free to students. The program pages do not say if students get paid.
duration: Runs year-round, with a six-week summer program on campus.
deadline_text: The pages disagree. The main page says applications are rolling with a May 31 deadline and gives no year. The FAQ says applications usually run mid-February through April, and the director may add other periods. Call to confirm.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Send papers that show you are eligible, like a report card, test scores and proof of income. Then you have a virtual interview. Questions: 215-204-3636.
notes: Federally funded. You must have a goal of going to college. Income is not the only factor in who is accepted. The FAQ also says 8th graders can apply in spring before high school. As of Nov 4, 2026, the Upward Bound Application page shows no form, only a general Temple Apply link, so call before you apply.
